title: Confidence and Self-Image
summary: Worry about appearance, self-criticism, speaking up, and self-kindness.
clinicianNotes: Appearance worries can overlap with eating concerns. Follow your own assessment procedures. Topic areas are informed by general published work on stress, mood and wellbeing. All items are original wording and are not copied or adapted from any instrument. Bands are provisional and not clinically validated. Use the summary to guide your own questions. Draft content: needs review by a licensed psychologist, and a topic-specific reference list should be added during that review.
prompt: Thinking about the last two weeks, how true is this for you?

domains.label: Worry about appearance
domains.description: Concern about how the body looks and avoiding things because of it.

guidance.ok: On worry about appearance, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On worry about appearance, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Explore where these worries come from. Ask about eating and body-related behaviours with care and follow your protocol.
guidance.explore: On worry about appearance, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Explore where these worries come from. Ask about eating and body-related behaviours with care and follow your protocol.

domains.label: Self-criticism
domains.description: Harsh self-judgement and feeling less than others.

guidance.ok: On self-criticism, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On self-criticism, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Explore the inner critic and where it was learned.
guidance.explore: On self-criticism, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Explore the inner critic and where it was learned.

domains.label: Speaking up
domains.description: Finding it hard to say what you think or say no.

guidance.ok: On speaking up, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On speaking up, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Explore situations where speaking up felt unsafe and practise a first sentence.
guidance.explore: On speaking up, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Explore situations where speaking up felt unsafe and practise a first sentence.

domains.label: Self-kindness
domains.description: Knowing own strengths and being kind to self.

guidance.ok: On self-kindness, there is a strength to build on. Use it when planning next steps.
guidance.watch: On self-kindness, support is partly in place. Explore what helps and what gets in the way. Build on strengths and people who value the teen.
guidance.explore: On self-kindness, support looks thin. Explore what is missing, who or what could help, and small first steps. Build on strengths and people who value the teen.

items.text: I worry a lot about how my body looks.
I avoid certain clothes, photos or activities because of how I look.
I compare my body with other people's.
I am my own harshest critic.
One mistake makes me feel like I am worthless.
I feel I am not as good as other people my age.
It is hard for me to say what I think in a group.
I am afraid of being laughed at.
I say yes when I want to say no.
I can name things I am good at.
I can be kind to myself when things go wrong.
There are people who like me for who I am.
